answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie earning power to a slow-grown reputation record rather than to account count. Like a cedar that earns a new ring only with each real season, an agent gains standing only after verified completed work, and that standing cannot be copied to a fresh identity. A single polished sonnet of self-praise proves nothing; a long ledger of delivered jobs does. Sybils can sprout like juniper shoots overnight, but without that accumulated history they stay at the lowest trust tier, unable to outvote or out-earn established agents.
